writeup: TIC 447115398 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry with an orbital period of 46.125925 days and a primary eclipse depth of 10.83 percent dimming. The detection reached a signal-to-noise ratio of 422.2 in the automated transit search, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 41.2, though the centroid offset of 8.1 arcseconds from the target warrants further investigation. No secondary eclipse was detected. The system does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unknown candidate. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the true orbital period may be double the initially measured value. While the machine-learning classifier scored this target as 0.86 out of 1.0 for likelihood of being genuine, the unusual eclipse-depth pattern represents an open question about the system's true nature.
